tasks.title: Implement the todo store in src/todos.js with node:test coverage
tasks.description: Create src/todos.js, a dependency-free ESM module holding all todo persistence and rendering, every function taking the store file path explicitly so it is testable without touching any fixed location. Create test/todos.test.js covering it.

context.reason: confirms "type": "module" ESM and the node --test runner used by the new tests
existing test style (node:test + node:assert/strict) to match in the new test file

edits.change:
Create an ESM module (no imports of project files; use `readFile`/`writeFile`/`mkdir` from `node:fs/promises` and `dirname` from `node:path`) exporting exactly these six functions:

- `readTodos(file)`: read `file` as UTF-8 JSON and return `parsed.todos`; if the file does not exist return `[]`. If the file exists but contains invalid JSON, throw an Error with message `Cannot parse todo store at <file>: <reason>`. If the parsed value is not an object or `todos` is not an array, throw an Error with message `Todo store at <file> is not a valid todo store`.
- `writeTodos(file, todos)`: `mkdir(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` then `writeFile(file, JSON.stringify({ todos }, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf8')`.
- `addTodo(file, text)`: `text` must be a string whose trimmed value is non-empty, otherwise throw an Error with message `Todo text cannot be empty`. Append `{ id: nextId, text: text.trim(), done: false }` where `nextId` is 1 when the existing list is empty, otherwise `Math.max(...existing.map(t => t.id)) + 1`. Write the file and return the new todo object `{ id, text, done }`.
- `completeTodo(file, id)`: find the todo whose `id` strictly equals `id` (callers pass numbers; `done <id>` and `remove <id>` are parsed with parseInt before being passed in); if none, throw an Error with message `Todo ${id} not found`. Set its `done` to true, write, and return the updated todo.
- `removeTodo(file, id)`: same lookup; if none, throw an Error with message `Todo ${id} not found`. Remove it from the array, write, and return the removed todo.
- `formatLines(todos, { pendingOnly = false } = {})`: return an array of strings, one per todo, each formatted as ``${todo.done ? '✔' : '  '} ${todo.id}. ${todo.text}`` (note: two leading spaces for a pending todo so columns align with the check mark). When `pendingOnly` is true, return only the lines whose todo has `done === false`.

Create a node:test file importing { test } from 'node:test', assert from 'node:assert/strict', { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises', { dirname, join } from 'node:path' and { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url', plus the six functions from '../src/todos.js'.

Define `const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` and an async helper `async function withStore(fn)` that calls `mkdtemp(join(here, '.tmp-todos-'))`, invokes `await fn(join(dir, 'todos.json'))`, and always `await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` in a `finally` block — so every fixture directory is created inside the project `test/` folder and is cleaned up even when a test fails.

Write these cases, each wrapping its body in `await withStore(async (file) => { ... })`:
1. 'appends a todo with an incrementing id': seed the file with `JSON.stringify({ todos: [{ id: 1, text: 'old', done: true }] })`, call `addTodo(file, 'buy milk')`, re-read the file, and assert the stored array deep-equals `[{ id: 1, text: 'old', done: true }, { id: 2, text: 'buy milk', done: false }]`.
2. 'starts ids at 1 when the store does not exist yet': call `addTodo(file, 'first')` with no file present, assert the returned id is 1 and done is false, and assert the file now exists.
3. 'trims the text and rejects empty text': assert `addTodo(file, '  spaced  ')` stores `text === 'spaced'`, and `await assert.rejects(() => addTodo(file, '   '), /cannot be empty/i)`.
4. 'completeTodo marks a todo done and rejects unknown ids': seed two todos, `completeTodo(file, 1)`, assert the stored first todo has `done === true`; `await assert.rejects(() => completeTodo(file, 99), /not found/i)`.
5. 'removeTodo deletes by id and rejects unknown ids': seed two todos, `removeTodo(file, 1)`, assert the stored array is exactly `[{ id: 2, ... }]`; `await assert.rejects(() => removeTodo(file, 99), /not found/i)`.
6. 'formatLines renders a check mark for done todos': assert `formatLines([{ id: 1, text: 'old', done: true }, { id: 2, text: 'new', done: false }])` deep-equals `['✔ 1. old', '  2. new']`.
7. 'formatLines with pendingOnly drops done todos': same input with `{ pendingOnly: true }` deep-equals `['  2. new']`.
8. 'readTodos throws a clear error for a corrupt store': write `{ not json` into the file and assert `assert.throws(() => readTodos(file), /Cannot parse todo store/)`.

tasks.title: Implement argument parsing and exit codes in src/todo-cli.js, plus bin/todo.js
tasks.description: Create src/todo-cli.js exporting an injectable run(argv, io) so tests can capture stdout/stderr and the exit code, and bin/todo.js as the executable shim. run() resolves the store path from process.env.TODOS_FILE at call time, falling back to DEFAULT_FILE — the project-root-relative `.todos.json`. The sandbox cannot write outside the project directory, so the default must be project-relative; it lives in one named constant so it can be repointed later without touching anything else.

context.reason: the store and formatLines API this task wires up
bin wiring goes here in the next task; confirms ESM so bin needs the .js extension

edits.change:
Create an ESM module with exactly one export: `export function run(argv, io = { stdout: process.stdout, stderr: process.stderr, env: process.env })`. It returns a number (the process exit code) instead of calling process.exit, and prints through io.stdout.write / io.stderr.write.

At the top of the file define the default store path as a single named constant, computed from this module's own location so it is independent of the working directory:
```js
const DEFAULT_FILE = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '.todos.json')
```
using `join`/`dirname` from 'node:path' and `fileURLToPath` from 'node:url' (no os.homedir, nothing outside the project).

Resolve the store path inside run, not at module load: `const file = io.env.TODOS_FILE || DEFAULT_FILE`. Return 0 on success, 1 on any user error (message on stderr, nothing on stdout).

USAGE text, printed to stderr for every error, and never to stdout:
```
Usage:
  todo add <text>      Add a todo
  todo list [--pending] List todos (--pending hides done ones)
  todo done <id>        Mark a todo as done
  todo remove <id>      Remove a todo

Todos are stored in .todos.json (override with TODOS_FILE)
```

Behaviour per argv (argv excludes node and script path; no argv or an empty array → usage error, return 1):
- `add`: require at least one text argument; join them with single spaces (`argv.slice(2).join(' ')`) so `todo add buy milk` stores `buy milk`. If none, write `Todo text cannot be empty` to stderr, then the usage block, and return 1. Otherwise call `addTodo(file, text)` and write `Added ${todo.id}: ${todo.text}\n` to stdout, return 0.
- `list`: accept either `['list']` or `['list', '--pending']`; pass `{ pendingOnly: true }` to formatLines in the second case. Write nothing at all to stdout when the resulting list is empty (not even a newline). Any other argument after `list` writes `Unknown option: ${arg}` to stderr, then the usage block, and returns 1. Otherwise write each line from formatLines(readTodos(file), opts) to stdout, each followed by a newline, and return 0.
- `done`: require exactly one argument; `const id = Number.parseInt(arg, 10)`; if `Number.isNaN(id)` write `Invalid id: ${arg}` to stderr, then usage, return 1. Otherwise call `completeTodo(file, id)` and write `Marked ${id} done\n` to stdout, return 0.
- `remove`: same id parsing, then `removeTodo(file, id)` and write `Removed ${id}\n` to stdout, return 0.
- any other first argument: write `Unknown command: ${cmd}` to stderr, then the usage block, return 1.

Wrap every store call in try/catch; on a caught error write `err.message` to stderr, then the usage block, and return 1. This covers the `Todo <id> not found` and `Todo text cannot be empty` errors thrown by src/todos.js.

Create a two-part executable shim: line 1 is exactly `#!/usr/bin/env node`, line 2 imports run from '../src/todo-cli.js' (ESM, so the .js extension is required) and calls it: `import { run } from '../src/todo-cli.js'` newline `process.exitCode = run(process.argv.slice(2))`. Nothing else in the file — all logic stays in src/todo-cli.js so it stays testable.

Create a node:test file importing { test } from 'node:test', assert from 'node:assert/strict', { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises', { dirname, join } from 'node:path', { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url' and { run } from '../src/todo-cli.js'.

Define `const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`, an async helper `async function withStore(fn)` using `mkdtemp(join(here, '.tmp-cli-'))` + `rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` in a finally block, a `seed(file, todos)` helper that writes `JSON.stringify({ todos }, null, 2)` to the file, and an io factory:
```js
function capture(file, argv) {
  const out = [], err = []
  const code = run(argv, {
    stdout: { write: (s) => { out.push(s); return true } },
    stderr: { write: (s) => { err.push(s); return true } },
    env: { TODOS_FILE: file }
  })
  return { code, stdout: out.join(''), stderr: err.join('') }
}
```
Every case passes an explicit `env: { TODOS_FILE: file }`, so no test ever writes to the project-root `.todos.json` default.

1. 'add creates the store and prints the new id': `const r = capture(file, ['add', 'buy milk'])`; assert `r.code === 0`, `r.stdout === 'Added 1: buy milk\n'`, and the stored todos deep-equal `[{ id: 1, text: 'buy milk', done: false }]`.

6. 'list --pending hides done todos': same seed, `capture(file, ['list', '--pending'])`; assert `r.stdout === '  2. new\n'`.
7. 'list prints nothing for an empty store': seed `[]`; assert `r.stdout === ''` and `r.code === 0`.
8. 'done marks the todo and prints a confirmation': seed two todos; `capture(file, ['done', '1'])` → `r.code === 0`, `r.stdout === 'Marked 1 done\n'`, and the stored first todo has `done === true`.
9. 'done with an unknown id fails': `capture(file, ['done', '99'])` → `r.code === 1`, `r.stdout === ''`, stderr matches `/not found/i`.
10. 'done with a non-numeric id fails': `capture(file, ['done', 'abc'])` → `r.code === 1`, stderr matches `/Invalid id/`.
11. 'remove deletes the todo': seed two todos; `capture(file, ['remove', '1'])` → `r.stdout === 'Removed 1\n'` and the stored todos deep-equal `[{ id: 2, text: 'new', done: false }]`.
12. 'remove with an unknown id fails': `capture(file, ['remove', '99'])` → `r.code === 1`, stderr matches `/not found/i`.
13. 'an unknown command fails with usage': `capture(file, ['bogus'])` → `r.code === 1`, `r.stdout === ''`, stderr matches `/Unknown command: bogus/` and `/Usage:/`.
14. 'an unknown list option fails': `capture(file, ['list', '--all'])` → `r.code === 1`, stderr matches `/Unknown option: --all/`.

Append two new sections after the existing Tests section, leaving the current text untouched. Add:

## todo

A small command-line todo list. Todos are stored as JSON in `.todos.json` at the
root of this project (the file is created on the first `add`).

Install it on your PATH with:

    npm link

### Usage

    todo add <text>        Add a todo (quote the text or pass several words)
    todo list              List all todos
    todo list --pending    List only todos that are not done yet
    todo done <id>         Mark a todo as done
    todo remove <id>       Delete a todo

A done todo is shown with a check mark:

    $ todo add buy milk
    Added 1: buy milk
    $ todo add write docs
    Added 2: write docs
    $ todo done 1
    Marked 1 done
    $ todo list
    ✔ 1. buy milk
      2. write docs
    $ todo list --pending
      2. write docs
    $ todo remove 2
    Removed 2

contracts.statement: Todos live in a single JSON file. src/todo-cli.js owns all location knowledge in one constant: `DEFAULT_FILE = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '.todos.json')`, i.e. the project-root-relative .todos.json, because nothing outside the project directory is reachable. run() resolves the store path at call time as `io.env.TODOS_FILE || DEFAULT_FILE` — never at module load — so the environment variable can repoint the list at another writable file. The file is UTF-8 JSON of the shape `{ "todos": [ { "id": 1, "text": "buy milk", "done": false } ] }`, written pretty-printed with a trailing newline. Ids are integers starting at 1 and are never reused: the next id is the max existing id plus 1, or 1 when the store is empty. A missing file reads as an empty list.

src/todo-cli.js exports exactly one function, `run(argv, io)`, where argv is the argument list with the command name included and the node/script paths already stripped (e.g. ['list', '--pending']), and io has the shape { stdout: { write }, stderr: { write }, env }. run() returns the exit code as a number (0 success, 1 user error) and never calls process.exit. Success output goes to stdout; every user-facing error message and the usage block go to stderr while stdout stays empty.

Every rendered list line is `${mark} ${id}. ${text}` followed by a newline, where mark is the check mark character '✔' (U+2714) for a done todo and exactly two spaces '  ' for a pending one, so ids and text stay column-aligned across mixed lists. `list --pending` renders only pending todos. An empty list prints nothing at all — not even a blank line.
